techniques.name: Expansive Open-String Drone Strumming
techniques.description: Placing a capo on the 4th fret allows guitarists to play familiar G, D, and C open shapes while anchoring 3rd and 4th fingers on strings 2 and 1 to create an unbroken acoustic shimmer

sequence: Affix capo to 4th fret and tune carefully
Anchor your pinky and ring fingers on frets 3 of strings 1 and 2 (relative to capo)
Transition only your index and middle fingers between G, Cadd9, and Em7
Maintain continuous, sweeping down-up 88 BPM strumming
tips: Keep the 3rd and 4th fingers anchored firmly — this creates the famous Coldplay acoustic bed
Use a thin or medium pick (0.50mm to 0.60mm) for smooth, sweeping strumming texture
Do not mute the high open strings; let them ring out as wide as possible

beginner.title: Master the Anchored Chords
steps: Place capo on 4th fret and tune carefully
Anchor 3rd and 4th fingers on strings 1 and 2 (3rd fret)
Practice transitioning between G, Cadd9, and Em7
Strum through the verse progression at 88 BPM

intermediate.title: Dynamic Control & Chorus Flow
steps: Master the chorus progression: Cadd9 → Em7 → D
Practice dynamic transitions from quiet verse to soaring chorus
Sing along while maintaining steady 16th-note strumming sway

advanced.title: Stadium Acoustic Performance
steps: Capture Chris Martin's emotive falsetto vocal transitions

commonMistakes: Lifting fingers 3 and 4 off strings 1 and 2 during chord transitions
Capo placed too far from the fretwire causing buzz
Strumming too aggressively on the verses — start gently and build dynamically
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Capo 4 tuning check and open chord warm-up
5 minutes: Anchored finger transition drill (G to Cadd9)
5 minutes: Chorus singing and playing integration
focusAreas: Dynamic build from verse to chorus
metronomeWork: Practice at 75 BPM to master the chord changes
Advance to target 88 BPM once rhythm is steady
Set metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4 to lock in the backbeat sway
